walkthroughs.body_html:
By 1953, Watson and Crick had the structure of DNA, but how it replicated was still open.

Three rival models:
- Conservative: parental helix stays intact; daughter is brand new
- Semiconservative: each daughter has one old + one new strand
- Dispersive: strands are patchwork of old + new along their length

In 1958, Meselson and Stahl grew E. coli for many generations in a medium with heavy nitrogen ¹⁵N → all DNA was heavy.

They transferred bacteria to a medium with light ¹⁴N and let them replicate.

DNA was extracted at each generation, then spun in a CsCl density gradient. DNA settled at a band whose position depended on its density.

After one round of replication: a single band at intermediate density.
→ Ruled out conservative (which predicted 2 bands: heavy + light)

After two rounds: two bands — one intermediate, one light.
→ Ruled out dispersive (which predicted a single, slightly lighter intermediate band)

Only semiconservative replication fits both results.
